exercise.name: Cable Bar Lateral Pulldown

reference.title: Cable Bar Lateral Pulldown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder adduction, scapular depression, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the bar down to the upper chest, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to the upper chest without swinging back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; 1 s pause at the chest

cues.text: Sit under the high pulley, feet flat, and hold the lat bar with an overhand grip about 1.5 times shoulder width; arms long overhead, chest up.
Breathe out; draw the shoulders down and pull the bar to the top of the chest, elbows sweeping down and slightly back, leaning back only a little.
Bar at the upper chest, elbows under the bar and by the sides, chest up to meet it.
Breathe in and let the bar rise under control until the arms are long and the shoulders lift slightly.
Brief stretch at the top, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far back and rowing the bar
mistakes.fix: Keep the lean small (about 10-15 degrees back) and pull down, not back.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the bar behind the neck
mistakes.fix: Pull to the front of the upper chest.

mistakes.mistake: Using momentum to swing the weight down
mistakes.fix: Control the whole rep; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bar fly up and the shoulders shrug at the top
mistakes.fix: Let the bar rise slowly with the arms long but the shoulders controlled.

kinematics.setup: Overhand, 78 cm between the hands on a 120 cm lat bar (shoulders 40 cm apart)
kinematics.norm: Overhand, about 1.5 times shoulder width (clinical opinion); in EMG studies a wide front grip loaded the lats as well as or better than narrower or behind-the-neck variations (Signorile 2002; Lehman 2004)
From nearly straight to about 90-120 degrees (clinical opinion)
From arms overhead to the elbows by the sides (clinical opinion)
Small backward lean, about 10-15 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s down, 0.4 s at the chest, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Bar Lateral Pulldown, video (movement reference)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the shoulder or elbow, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control up and down without swinging.
Pull to the front of the chest, not behind the neck, and keep the head out of the bar's path.
This model sits on a plain box without the machine's thigh pads; with heavy loads use a machine with thigh pads so the body stays down.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: use a narrower, neutral (palms-facing) grip and a shorter top range (clinical opinion).
Elbow discomfort: lighten the load and loosen the grip slightly.
